status_summary: No federal law restricting addictive design features for minors has been enacted as of 2026-10-09. The House passed the KIDS Act (H.R. 7757), an omnibus of 14 bills that limits features such as push notifications, autoplay and infinite scroll for minors and bars targeted advertising to minors, on 2026-06-29; the Senate Commerce Committee approved the Kids Online Safety Act by voice vote on 2026-08-05, and Senate sponsors reject the House version because it omits a duty of care. The FTC's amended COPPA Rule (effective 2025-06-23, compliance 2026-04-22) and the TAKE IT DOWN Act (platform removal duties effective 2026-05-19) are operative but address privacy and non-consensual intimate images, not dependency. The FTC held a workshop on 2025-06-04 on how large technology firms exploit children and ordered seven companies on 2025-09-11 to report on AI companion chatbots and minors.

timeline.event: FTC publishes amended COPPA Rule (effective 2025-06-23; compliance date 2026-04-22): adds biometric identifiers to personal information and new consent methods; it did not adopt a proposed ban on using persistent identifiers to encourage use of a site.

FTC holds a workshop titled The Attention Economy: How Big Tech Firms Exploit Children and Hurt Families on habit-forming design, parental authority and possible roles for the FTC, Congress and states.

FTC orders Alphabet, Character Technologies, Instagram, Meta, OpenAI, Snap and xAI to provide information on how their AI companion chatbots affect children and teens, including age restrictions and COPPA compliance.

The House Energy and Commerce Committee approves the KIDS Act (H.R. 7757, folding in the House version of the Kids Online Safety Act), Sammy's Law and the App Store Accountability Act (H.R. 3149) along party lines; the House COPPA 2.0 bill was pulled from the markup.

The notice-and-removal duties of the TAKE IT DOWN Act (signed May 2025) take effect for covered platforms: reported non-consensual intimate images, including AI-generated ones, must be removed within 48 hours, with FTC enforcement and civil penalties. The law addresses intimate imagery, not platform dependency.

The House passes the amended KIDS Act (H.R. 7757), which combines 14 bills, restricts push notifications, autoplay and infinite scrolling for minors, bans targeted advertising to minors, regulates AI chatbots and omits the Kids Online Safety Act duty of care; Senate sponsors say it cannot pass the Senate in that form.
The Senate Commerce Committee approves the Kids Online Safety Act by unanimous voice vote and sends it to the full Senate; sponsors say they will not accept the House version.

title: Stop social media platforms from fostering dependency in children
uncertainties: No primary congress.gov page could be opened (robots restrictions), so bill status rests on news and law-firm sources; the House vote tally of 267 to 117 comes from an aggregator and Crowell gives no tally, and one report dates House passage to July while two give 2026-06-29. No full Senate vote on the Kids Online Safety Act after the 2026-08-05 committee vote was found in a limited search. The TAKE IT DOWN Act signing date is given only as May 2025 in the source read. The Foreword names no mechanism, so the stage reflects the closest checkable actions; the FTC COPPA amendments and TAKE IT DOWN Act are privacy and image-abuse measures, counted only as adjacent. State laws and litigation against platforms are outside federal action and were not tracked. Related record c30-03 covers FTC action on minors in more detail. The stage was moved in review from in_progress to proposed because the only measures aimed at platform dependency are bills that have not been enacted and FTC information-gathering steps; the operative COPPA and TAKE IT DOWN measures address other harms.
